data.summary: The "opencode" directory is a single scenario definition in what appears to be an aio-config scenario registry, declaring how to install the opencode AI coding agent into a container image. It contains only declarative artifacts: a scenario.toml metadata file consumed by `aio-config gen`, and a fragment.Dockerfile holding the actual mise-based install and verification steps. Together they form a self-contained, idempotent install unit whose success is gated by a login-shell PATH probe that auto-enables the app panel button.

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile fragment that installs the opencode AI coding agent via mise's aqua backend and verifies the binary is resolvable in a login shell.
file_insights.source_summary: A short Dockerfile fragment: an `ARG OPENCODE_VERSION={{version}}` placeholder, a `RUN mise use -g "opencode@${OPENCODE_VERSION}"` install step, a `mise ls opencode` listing for the build log, and a `bash -lc 'command -v opencode >/dev/null || { echo "MISSING(login): opencode" >&2; exit 1; }'` guard followed by a non-login `bash -c` check.
file_insights.detailed_description: This fragment is the executable half of the opencode scenario: it takes the OPENCODE_VERSION build arg injected from scenario.toml and runs `mise use -g opencode@${OPENCODE_VERSION}` to install the ~177MB aqua-backed binary into /opt/mise/installs. After installation it asserts both `mise ls opencode` and a login-shell `command -v opencode` check, failing the build with a MISSING(login) message if the binary is not on the login PATH. That guard is intentional because the app panel's opencode button (type=agent) is enabled only when command_exists(opencode) succeeds, so a successful build makes the button appear and a failed one keeps it hidden rather than producing a dead pane.
responsibilities: Install the opencode binary globally via mise/aqua at the version passed in as a build arg
Verify the install with `mise ls opencode` for build-time observability
Assert that opencode resolves on the login-shell PATH so the app panel button activates
Fail fast with an explicit error if the binary is missing, keeping the UI free of dead panes

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Scenario metadata file declaring the opencode install scenario's id, category, installer, and pinned version for `aio-config gen` fragment resolution.
file_insights.source_summary: A declarative TOML document with top-level keys `id = "opencode"`, `name = "opencode"`, a description explaining the aqua-backed agent install (~177MB, /opt/mise/installs) and the command -v button guard, `category = "app"`, `installer = "mise"`, and one `[[versions]]` entry with label and version both set to "1.18.24".
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the registry entry that the aio-config generator reads to discover the opencode scenario and pair it with the sibling fragment.Dockerfile. It declares id/name "opencode" (matching the resulting binary name), category "app", installer "mise", and a single versions block pinning 1.18.24 with a matching human-readable label. Its description also documents the command -v guard behavior that hides the app panel button when the tool is absent.
responsibilities: Identify the scenario uniquely via id/name for fragment resolution
Classify the scenario as an app-layer install backed by the mise installer
Pin the installable version (1.18.24) exposed to the Dockerfile build arg
Document the UI guard semantics that hide the app panel button when opencode is not installed
